evidence.text: Topics. the ROI of conversion rate optimization / arguing that doubling conversion rates is vastly superior to doubling traffic because it amplifies the return on all existing ad spend and lowers customer acquisition costs; above the fold structure / defining the essential elements: benefit-driven headline, pain-to-solution sub-headline, stacked social proof, FUD reducers (fear, uncertainty, doubt), and a reinforcing image; traffic-aware sequencing / matching the page layout to the audience's awareness level (e.g., placing the "Pain/Proof" section first for problem-aware Meta Ads traffic, but placing "Social Proof" first for solution-aware Google Ads traffic); data analysis with Microsoft Clarity / a tutorial on using session recordings, scroll maps, and click maps to identify user drop-offs, rage clicks, and ignored CTA buttons, leading to immediate UX fixes like removing navigation bars; qualitative user testing / using UserBrain to recruit targeted demographics to perform specific tasks on the site while narrating their thought process aloud; WordPress and Elementor setup / the technical stack recommendation of using Flywheel for premium hosting and Elementor Pro for flexible, custom landing page development; deploying A/B tests with FigPii / a walkthrough of setting up visual A/B tests (changing headlines via the editor) versus split URL tests (routing traffic 50/50 to completely different page URLs), emphasizing that testing is only viable for sites with over 25,000 monthly visitors.

cards.title: Traffic-aware page sequencing by audience awareness
cards.claim: Match landing page layout to the audience's awareness level: place the "Pain/Proof" section first for problem-aware Meta Ads traffic, but place "Social Proof" first for solution-aware Google Ads traffic.
cards.action: Order page sections according to traffic source awareness: for problem-aware Meta Ads traffic put the "Pain/Proof" section first; for solution-aware Google Ads traffic put "Social Proof" first.
applies_when: Serving Meta Ads traffic that is problem-aware
Serving Google Ads traffic that is solution-aware
do_not_use_when: Traffic source is not one of the described segments
unknowns: How to classify awareness level precisely
Whether ordering effects were tested or measured
Whether results generalize beyond these ad sources
evidence_quotes: traffic-aware sequencing / matching the page layout to the audience's awareness level (e.g., placing the "Pain/Proof" section first for problem-aware Meta Ads traffic, but placing "Social Proof" first for solution-aware Google Ads traffic)

cards.title: Essential above-the-fold elements
cards.claim: The essential above-the-fold structure includes a benefit-driven headline, a pain-to-solution sub-headline, stacked social proof, FUD reducers (fear, uncertainty, doubt), and a reinforcing image.
cards.action: Include a benefit-driven headline, pain-to-solution sub-headline, stacked social proof, FUD reducers, and a reinforcing image in the above-the-fold structure.
applies_when: Designing a landing page's above-the-fold section
do_not_use_when: The page has constraints that prevent one or more listed elements
unknowns: Which element drives the most impact
Whether all five elements are required in every context
evidence_quotes: above the fold structure / defining the essential elements: benefit-driven headline, pain-to-solution sub-headline, stacked social proof, FUD reducers (fear, uncertainty, doubt), and a reinforcing image

cards.title: A/B testing only viable above 25k monthly visitors
cards.claim: Testing is only viable for sites with over 25,000 monthly visitors.
cards.action: Consider A/B testing only if the site has over 25,000 monthly visitors.
applies_when: Deciding whether to run A/B tests
do_not_use_when: Site traffic is below the stated threshold
unknowns: The basis or derivation of the 25,000-visitor threshold
Whether the threshold varies by test type or conversion rate
evidence_quotes: emphasizing that testing is only viable for sites with over 25,000 monthly visitors
